name: Black-cowled Saltator
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of southern ecuador and northwestern peru
description: Handsome gray-and-black cloud forest bird with a stout orange bill. It has a very restricted range in the Andes of northwestern Peru and southwestern Ecuador.

name: Maui Alauahio
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of eastern maui
description: A small Hawaiian honeycreeper of native forests above 5,000 feet elevation on eastern Maui. Occurs in non-native forest at Poli-Poli.

name: Greater Yellow-Finch
rangeDescription: Andes of northern and central chile and adjacent argentina
description: Fairly common in the Andes of central Chile and adjacent Argentina; seen readily at ski resorts, around villages, on bogs, and on stony and grassy slopes. Often in flocks, associates readily with other seed-eating birds.

name: Royal Penguin
rangeDescription: Macquarie island and adjacent islets
description: The largest crested penguin, with a diagnostic whitish face. Only breeds on the Australian-administered Macquarie Island; occasionally seen off of New Zealand’s subantarctic islands, rarely off of the mainland.

name: Finsch's Euphonia
rangeDescription: Southeastern venezuela to the guianas and northern brazil (northern roraima)
description: Small finch of forest canopy; often seen perched on bare branches. Males have yellow forecrown and belly contrasting with dark throat; females mostly dull yellow and green.

name: Nicobar Serpent-Eagle
rangeDescription: Great nicobar island (nicobar islands)
description: A very small eagle distinguished by its size, black crest, pale brown plumage, and completely unmarked underparts. Restricted to the Nicobar Islands, where it is similar to the Crested Serpent-Eagle, but the Nicobar Serpent-Eagle is much smaller and lacks any spots on the belly.

name: Coscoroba Swan
rangeDescription: Southern brazil to paraguay, uruguay, tierra del fuego, and falkland islands
description: A distinctive white swan with a bright, rather ducklike bill. The black wingtips are usually concealed when swimming.

name: Enggano Imperial-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Enggano island (off southwestern sumatra)
description: Large pigeon from Enggano island off Sumatra. Other than deep green wings and back, predominantly pale gray, though slightly darker on the back of the neck.

name: Caspian Plover
rangeDescription: Caspian sea to far western china; winters in eastern and southern africa
description: Stately plover with a gentle, dovelike expression. Breeding male is stunning, with a white face and belly separated by a broad chestnut patch across the chest.

name: Black Manakin
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to southern venezuela, northeastern bolivia, and southern amazonian brazil
description: Small bird of dry scrub enclaves in rainforest regions. All-black male is distinctive; compared to other manakins, note longish tail and blue bill in both sexes.

name: Paradise Riflebird
rangeDescription: Eastern australia (dawes range, queensland to bellinger river, new south wales)
description: Large songbird with a very long decurved bill. Male almost completely black, with green and blue metallic sheen on belly, throat, and crown.

name: Chinese Sparrowhawk
rangeDescription: China and korea; winters to southeastern asia, philippines, and indonesia
description: Attractive accipiter of wooded habitats. Adult gray above with orange-suffused white underparts; also note bright yellow cere (skin around the nostrils).

name: Gray-breasted Crake
rangeDescription: Guatemala and belize to northern bolivia, and amazonian and eastern brazil
description: Very small and elusive crake of damp grassy fields, brushy pastures, and marshes. Walks quietly and runs quickly, like all rails.

name: Palani Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Southern india (palni and anaimalai hills and northern kerala)
description: This is the only montane laughingthrush in its range and hence unmistakable. It has dull olive-brown upperparts, a grey-streaked white breast, and a rufous-chestnut lower breast and belly.

name: Choco Poorwill
rangeDescription: Western colombia (chocó) and far northwestern ecuador
description: Dark brown night bird of humid forest in lowlands and foothills. Choco refers to its geographical range in western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador.

name: Rock Kestrel
rangeDescription: Northern angola to southern democratic republic of the congo, southern tanzania, and south africa
description: Typical kestrel with a rufous back and underparts, barred tail, and a dark “moustache” mark on the face. Found in a wide variety of open habitats, especially in rocky areas.

name: Maquis Canastero
rangeDescription: Andes of western bolivia (la paz and cochabamba)
description: Slender and long-tailed canastero of the high Andes from Cochabamba, Bolivia south to NE Argentina. Prefers scrubby hillsides, ravines, and open Polylepis woodland above treeline.

name: Trindade Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds trindade and martim vaz islands (south atlantic ocean)
description: A medium-sized gadfly petrel with long, pointed wings, long tail, and elastic, powerful flight. Bill is short and thick.

name: Rennell Shrikebill
rangeDescription: Rennell (southeastern solomon islands)
description: A large orange-brown bird with a black mask and a long, slightly decurved grayish-blue bill. Note the pale tuft at the “armpit.” Found mainly in the dense, tangled understory of primary forest.

name: Burchell's Starling
rangeDescription: Southern angola to western zambia, namibia, mozambique, and northern south africa
description: A large, long-tailed, iridescent blue-green to purple glossy starling with barred wings, and a round-tipped tail. Pairs, groups, and small flocks are resident in dry savanna, especially near thorn trees, where they have become common in camps and often associate with humans.
